headline: Over 5 lakh fail as HSC pass rate hits 22-year low
summary: The pass rate for general education boards dropped to 51.62%, the lowest since 2004, while GPA-5 achievers also hit an eight-year low.
details: The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with over 5,07,281 students failing under the nine general education boards.
The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, a significant drop from 57.12 percent last year, according to the results published on Saturday.
Data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS) reveals that the last time the pass rate was this low was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.
Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, the total number of failures increased to 5,94,113 students, compared to 5,08,701 last year.
The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also plummeted to an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving it across all 11 boards.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government will take steps to address learning gaps.
caption:

headline_marked: 30 [[garment factories suspend operations]] amid worker unrest
headline: 30 garment factories suspend operations amid worker unrest
summary: Workers in Ashulia and Mirpur are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and an end to blacklisting.
details: At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara in Ashulia have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
The unrest began in the morning, leading to clashes between workers and police. A police member was hospitalized after being struck on the head by bricks allegedly thrown by protesters.
In the Kathgara area, workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopped work before expanding their protest, allegedly throwing bricks and stones at nearby factories.
Protests also spread to Dhaka’s Mirpur area, where RMG workers blocked several roads to demand higher wages and an end to arbitrary dismissals.
Industrial police recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia around noon.
The Labour Minister announced that the process of forming a minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, though workers continue to protest as the message has not reached them all.
The Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre stated that the delay in forming the wage board, previously promised for October, fueled the anger.
caption:
30 garment factories shut down as workers demand a minimum wage of Tk 30,000.

At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara in Ashulia have declared a holiday today following protests by workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The unrest began in the morning, leading to clashes between workers and police. A police member was hospitalized after being struck on the head by bricks allegedly thrown by protesters.

In the Kathgara area, workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopped work before expanding their protest, allegedly throwing bricks and stones at nearby factories.

Protests also spread to Dhaka’s Mirpur area, where RMG workers blocked several roads to demand higher wages and an end to arbitrary dismissals.

Industrial police recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in the Nishchintapur area of Ashulia around noon.

The Labour Minister announced that the process of forming a minimum wage board would begin by Sunday, though workers continue to protest as the message has not reached them all.

The Bangladesh Garments and Sweaters Workers Trade Union Centre stated that the delay in forming the wage board, previously promised for October, fueled the anger.
